instructions: Ask the butcher to slice the beef, or cut it yourself across the grain into 6 pieces about 1/2 inch thick. Pat them dry and season with 1 teaspoon of the salt and the pepper.
Slice the garlic thinly. Chop the parsley. Warm the broth in a small pot or in the microwave.
Put the flour on a plate. Dredge each piece of beef in it and shake off the extra.
Heat the butter and 3 tablespoons of the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Brown the beef in 2 batches, 2 to 3 minutes a side, until golden. Transfer each batch to a plate.
Turn the heat down to medium, add the remaining 1 tablespoon oil and the garlic, and stir for 30 seconds, until it smells good but isn't brown.
Pour in the vinegar and scrape up the browned bits. Return the beef, add the wine, and let it bubble for 2 minutes.
Add the broth and the remaining 1 teaspoon salt. Bring to a simmer, then turn the heat down to medium-low, cover, and cook for 35 to 40 minutes, until the beef is tender and the sauce is thickened.
Meanwhile, put the rice in a pot with 2 cups of water. Bring to a boil, turn it down to low, cover, and cook for 15 minutes. Leave it covered off the heat until the beef is ready.
Stir the parsley into the skillet 5 minutes before the beef is done.
Taste it, and add a pinch more salt if it's flat. Serve with the rice.
method_notes: Lead is My Greek Dish (4.90 from 619): flour-dusted veal browned, then simmered in garlic, vinegar, white wine and beef broth with parsley added near the end. The source uses veal top round for 6; this uses beef top round, which the sources say is the common modern swap, and is scaled for four. Rice is the side, one of the three serving options in the lead (mashed potatoes, rice or fries). It runs about 65 minutes, a little over an hour.
